authors: Doh-Shin Jeon; Domenico Menicucci; Nikrooz Nasr
title: Compatibility Choices, Switching Costs, and Data Portability
setting: Two firms selling complementary products in a dynamic two-period market
method: Theory; simultaneous initial compatibility choice and dynamic price competition analyzed with SPNE
relevant_finding: High switching costs and sufficient patience can support incompatibility; data portability reduces switching costs and can make compatibility more likely; consumer effects are conditional
safe_claim: Firms may strategically choose incompatibility, and reducing switching costs through data portability can alter compatibility incentives in this model
unsafe_claim: The paper studies AI assistants, private implementation costs, a static Bayesian game, or our exact equilibrium multiplicity
project_connection: Closest strategic analogue to the Portable/Locked choice
project_difference: Uses complementary products, dynamic pricing, and SPNE; portability is a reduction in switching cost rather than a privately costly platform action
supports_section: Motivation; game theory; mechanism design; limitations
verification_source: AEA article record and abstract; author-posted TSE full-text working version for timing and solution concept

title: Coordination and Lock-In: Competition with Switching Costs and Network Effects
venue: Handbook of Industrial Organization, vol. 3, ch. 31, pp. 1967-2072
setting: General markets with switching costs or proprietary network effects
relevant_finding: Incompatibility can bind customers, create ex post market power, soften competition, and magnify incumbency advantages, but ex ante competition can sometimes be fierce
safe_claim: Switching costs can create lock-in and alter competition; effects are model-dependent rather than mechanically anticompetitive
unsafe_claim: This source establishes a specific result or parameter for AI-assistant memory portability
project_connection: Economic foundation for lock-in and strategic resistance to compatibility
project_difference: Broad survey, not an AI model and not a private-cost Bayesian game
supports_section: Motivation; game theory; real-world impact; limitations
verification_source: ScienceDirect chapter record; Elsevier volume record; Crossref DOI record

title: Do Switching Costs Make Markets More or Less Competitive? The Case of 800-Number Portability
method: Empirical analysis of price responses under uniform pricing
relevant_finding: AT&T and MCI reduced toll-free-service prices after portability; larger contracts saw larger price drops, consistent with greater prior lock-in
safe_claim: Reduced switching costs strengthened price competition in this portability setting; larger contracts had larger price declines
unsafe_claim: The magnitude applies to AI assistants or portability always intensifies competition
project_connection: Empirical analogy for lower switching friction and competition
project_difference: Telecommunications prices and number portability, not AI memory or platform implementation choices
verification_source: Wiley journal article page and abstract

title: Data Portability and Interoperability Between Digital Platforms
literature_category: Digital platforms; portability; interoperability; security risk
setting: Two-period Hotelling duopoly with switching costs and network benefits
method: Theory with rational expectations, price competition, breach risk, care, and liability extensions
relevant_finding: Without breaches, regulation improves modeled welfare by reducing switching costs and increasing network benefits; with breaches, it raises accident probability, while suitable liability can induce efficient care
safe_claim: Portability/interoperability can bring competition and network benefits while creating data-breach risk in this model
unsafe_claim: Portability always increases welfare or is costless and risk-free
project_connection: Adds a digital-platform welfare and security limitation
project_difference: Regulated interoperability with homogeneous switching costs, not voluntary AI portability with private implementation costs
verification_source: Wiley article page and full open-access text; formal issue 2026, online 21 May 2025

title: Status Quo Bias in Decision Making
setting: Decision experiments and real choices including faculty health and retirement plans
method: Experimental and observational evidence with theoretical discussion
relevant_finding: Choices disproportionately favor the status quo in the studied settings
safe_claim: Status quo bias provides a reason to test whether persistence remains after technical switching friction falls
unsafe_claim: AI-assistant users or our future participants exhibit status quo bias
project_connection: Motivates a planned Stay/Switch behavioral hypothesis
project_difference: General decision settings; no AI-assistant switching evidence

title: Counterspeculation, Auctions, and Competitive Sealed Tenders
relevant_finding: Provides the classic second-price sealed-bid foundation and truthful-bidding benchmark under private values
safe_claim: A second-price auction supplies a standard truthful-bidding benchmark under the usual private-value assumptions
unsafe_claim: Our switching-hurdle reserve design or exact first-price-with-reserve formula comes from Vickrey
project_difference: Does not study portability, AI users, or our reserve calibration

title: Optimal Auction Design
setting: One object, multiple buyers, seller imperfectly informed about willingness to pay
method: Optimal mechanism design using Nash equilibrium
relevant_finding: Derives optimal auctions for a broad class of single-object auction-design problems
safe_claim: Auction design can be framed as allocation and payment design under private information
unsafe_claim: The project implements Myerson's optimal auction
project_difference: Our project compares two standard auction formats and does not solve the Myerson optimization problem

title: Data Portability, Interoperability and Competition
venue: OECD Roundtables on Competition Policy Papers No. 260
method: Policy synthesis and competition roundtable background
relevant_finding: Portability may reduce switching costs; interoperability may aid multihoming and preserve network effects; implementation raises legal, technical, and data-protection challenges
safe_claim: Portability and interoperability are policy tools that may promote competition but require careful implementation
unsafe_claim: This report is peer-reviewed causal evidence or proves welfare effects for AI assistants
project_difference: Not a peer-reviewed model or empirical estimate
verification_source: Official OECD publication and roundtable pages

title: Competition When Consumers Have Switching Costs: An Overview with Applications to Industrial Organization, Macroeconomics, and International Trade
setting: Markets in which consumers face supplier-switching costs
relevant_finding: Installed share affects future profitability; firms trade off harvesting locked-in buyers against investing to win future customers
safe_claim: Switching costs can alter pricing, market-share investment, entry, and product choice
unsafe_claim: Switching costs always raise prices or this paper models AI assistants
project_connection: Concise classic support for the lock-in narrative
project_difference: General survey and partly redundant with Farrell and Klemperer
verification_source: Oxford Academic article and issue records
